title: Location: Tiny Island. Population: YOU
description:
It’s something you might dream of - or only see in films or read in books - moving to a remote island in the middle of the sea. Only wildlife around you. No bars or clubs and barely any people!

Sound like a bit of you? Or maybe it’s your worst nightmare. We speak to BBC reporter Georgina Rannard, about why she’s swapping city life to be a farmer on an island in Wales with only three other people. We also hear tips from people that’ve done similar things. Jaleesah lives on Siquijor in the Philippines and Tom works on a research station in Antarctica.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討前 BBC 氣候與科學記者 Georgina Rannard 離開城市的媒體工作，與伴侶一同搬遷至人口僅有 4 人的威爾斯巴德西島，轉行從事保育農業的故事。該島氣候多風多雨且無公共電網，生活需依靠太陽能板與發電機，補給則全仰賴船隻運送，冬季極端天氣下甚至可能斷航長達 6 週。節目亦邀請住在菲律賓的 Jaleesah 與在南極研究站工作的 Tom 分享偏遠生活的建議，包含透過語音或影片訊息與親友聯繫、攜帶安慰心靈的家鄉物品，以及在遭遇挑戰時回想當初選擇改變生活的初衷。
summaryEn: In this podcast episode, BBC climate and science correspondent Georgina Rannard discusses her transition from city life to becoming a conservation farmer on Bardsey Island (Ynys Enlli) in Wales, joining a permanent population of just four people. She details the realities of living off-grid—such as relying on solar power, generators, and outdoor toilets—and managing conservation farming to protect local seabirds and plant life despite harsh weather that can cut off boat deliveries for weeks. The episode also features insights from individuals living in remote parts of the Philippines and Antarctica, who share tips on staying connected through voice notes, bringing comforting items from home, and holding onto one's core motivation when facing major life changes.
